settings.name_in_paper: Slowly-varying two-armed non-stationary bandits with drift limit delta
unmapped: Per-round drift limit: |mu_{a,t} - mu_{a,t+1}| <= delta_drift for every arm and round (implies variation budget V_T = T*delta_drift)
The learner knows the drift limit delta_drift (or an upper bound on it)
Rewards independent over time, drawn from Bernoulli(mu_{a,t}) with time-varying means fixed in advance
settings.definition_quote: A bandit instance $\mu$ is defined to be \emph{slowly-varying} with \emph{drift limit} $\delta > 0$ (denoted as $\mu \in S_\delta$) if the expected reward profile satisfies \forall a \in \Arms, t \in [T-1], \abs{\mu_{a,t}-\mu_{a,t+1}} \leq \delta. ... We assume that the algorithm has access to the drift limit $\delta$ (or a suitable upper bound on it).

symbols.delta_drift: per-round drift limit on each arm's mean reward
symbols.sum_inv_lambda: sum over blocks j=1..m of 1/lambda_min(j), where lambda_min(j) is the minimum detectable gap lambda_t over block j; blocks have length tau = min{T, c_3 delta_drift^(-2/3) log^(1/3) T}

tuning: algorithm run with drift limit parameter delta_drift

source.label: thm:inst-dep-reg
source.quote: If $\AlgGE$ is run with a drift limit parameter $\delta$ on a problem instance $\mu \in S_\delta$, then its expected regret satisfies R(\AlgGE) \leq c_8 + c_6 \sum_{j=1}^{m} \frac{1}{\lambda_{min}(j)}. \log T + c_7, where $m = T/\tau$ is the number of blocks, each of length not more than $\tau = \min\{T, c_3 \delta^{-2/3} \log^{1/3} T\}$ ... $\lambda_{min}(j) := \min_{t \in b_j}\lambda_t$.

results.notes: Detectable gap profile lambda_t is defined in eq. (lamdba-curve). The appendix gives c_6=144, c_7=2, c_8=2. Claim 6 omits log T, while its proof and Theorem 1 include it; recorded as in the theorem. The constant c_7 may need to be summed per block (the proof is loose). Regret is defined via means against the per-round optimal arm, i.e. dynamic pseudo-regret.

symbols.delta_drift: per-round drift limit on each arm's mean reward

tuning: algorithm run with drift limit parameter delta_drift

source.label: thm:minimax-bound
source.quote: If $\AlgGE$ is run with a drift limit parameter $\delta$ on a problem instance $\mu \in S_\delta$, $\AlgGE$ incurs an expected regret of $O\left(T \delta^{1/3} \log^{1/3} T \right)$.

results.notes: Worst case over S_delta. Matches Besbes et al. with V_T = T*delta.

symbols.delta_drift: per-round drift limit on each arm's mean reward

conditions: hard instances: Bernoulli arms, one arm fixed at 1/2, the other drifting up and back within blocks of size m with eps = sqrt(1/(4m))

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: For any algorithm $\Alg$ and a drift limit $\delta > 0$, there exists a problem instance $\mu \in S_\delta$ such that, $\Alg$ incurs a expected regret of $\Omega\left(T \delta^{1/3}\right)$.

results.notes: Proof uses a non-stationary change-of-measure inequality on a block construction. Implicitly needs the block size m <= T, i.e. delta not too small relative to T.
